scope: Read-only source and official-contract review. The mechanism is possible; this run has not been shown to exercise it. No production process-launch changes or remote experiment were performed.

rustSource.lineNumberBasis: Original downloaded UTF-8 source, including blank lines; browser rendering may renumber lines.

facts.finding: Ordinary spawn supplies no process-thread attribute list.
The standard library's private CREATE_PROCESS_LOCK serializes its own spawn implementation; the product's raw native CreateProcessW does not acquire it.
Only an explicitly supplied attribute list selects STARTUPINFOEX; ordinary spawn uses STARTUPINFO.
CreateProcessW receives the inherit_handles flag. Ordinary spawn therefore has TRUE inheritance without a HANDLE_LIST.

windowsContracts.finding: TRUE inheritance includes inheritable handles in the calling process. The API documents multithreaded inheritance concerns and an explicit per-launch handle list. A strict list on one launch does not constrain another launch.
HANDLE_LIST handles must still be inheritable. This leaves a window during which another TRUE-inheritance launch without a list could receive them.

nativePipeWindow.finding: CreatePipe initially makes both ends inheritable, then clears inheritance on the parent end. The child stdin/stdout/stderr ends remain inheritable through CreateProcessW and close by local RAII on launch_entry return. The raw launch has a strict three-handle list, fresh AppContainer and creation-time Job. It does not share the standard library spawn mutex.

nativeLaunchConcurrency.finding: The product manages one native Registry. Its active flag remains set throughout backend rendering and cleanup; queued calls wait. Normal product native launches therefore do not overlap. Independently, two correctly configured HANDLE_LIST launches would each inherit only their selected handles. Separate application processes have separate handle tables.

webViewAndWorkers.finding: The locked Wry source calls CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions and controller COM APIs; it does not expose the Runtime's underlying process creation flags or handle list. Plugin Workers use the existing WebView's JavaScript Worker API, not a Rust Command call. Browser-side child creation cannot directly inherit a later handle that exists only in the product process. Product-side Runtime creation or recovery during the window remains unmeasured, and its inheritance policy is unknown from this source.

optionalDeterministicControl.design: A cfg(test)-only Windows fixture could hold a synthetic inheritable pipe writer across a barrier, start one fixed owned child with ordinary Command and a fixed control with a strict HANDLE_LIST excluding that writer, then close the parent's writer. Check actual pipe completion while each known child remains alive and after its bounded termination. Stop and clean only these fixture children. No Mermaid source, Runtime, token changes, global handle enumeration or arbitrary command is needed.
optionalDeterministicControl.limit: This would verify the mechanism under the pinned toolchain, not prove overlap or identify a leaking process in run 41692476025. It must not delay the observability patch and actual product acceptance.
